text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Some 210 members of the Church of the Province of Kenya (Anglican) electoral college are to meet on Wednesday to elect a new archbishop.
- In its November bulletin, the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR says Kenya's refugee population has gradually fallen from 420,000 in 1992 to 168,000 today.
- Two policemen are gunned down by robbers in the town of Sagana in central Kenya. Robbers escape with 3.4 million shillings belonging to an oil company.
- More than 150 students from Moi University demonstrate in Eldoret town after two of them are beaten up by security guards for alleged shop lifting.

- Raila Odinga, a faction leader in the opposition FORD-Kenya party, says the opposition will boycott and disrupt the coming general elections if constitutional changes are not made and the electoral commission reconstituted.
- Kenya and Uganda governments will establish a joint peace council early next year to maintain peace and stop cattle rustling among pastoral tribes occupying the common border region.
- High Court allows Kenya Cooperative Creameries and Kenya Dairy Board to carry on negotiations aimed at resolving the issue of decentralising KCC assets and selling them to farmers.
